notes: docs/isa.md: a missing key, or a target that is neither map nor list, pushes :undefined - never an error
docs/isa.md: negative indices are not supported and push :undefined rather than indexing from the end
a key that is not a string, integer, or atom is a TypeMismatchError - unlike a missing key or an out-of-range index, which are undefined
docs/isa.md: a list accepts only a non-negative integer index; every other key type, including boolean, is a TypeMismatchError rather than a miss

docs/isa.md: a boolean is an accepted map key type; a miss pushes :undefined rather than a TypeMismatchError. The hit case (a map with an actual boolean key) is not encodable here - JSON object keys are strings and the tagged-value encoding has no boolean-keyed map form - so it stays an Elixir-side test instead

docs/isa.md: make_list reverses the stack (deepest first) back into source order; an all-literal list compiles to a single lit instead, so at least one non-literal element is needed to force this opcode
count: 0 is reachable only from a hand-built instruction list - the compiler never emits make_list for an empty literal list, which compiles to ["lit", []] instead

an absent key compared against the undefined literal - the boundness test px-ocp exists for. The literal lowers to lit, never load, so it is unaffected by on_unbound (an evaluation option outside this corpus's scope)

px-o9v: a present key bound to null is not a missing key - the statifier bug this case pins. Contrast with access/missing-key-strict-eq-undefined-literal, whose key is genuinely absent and answers true

px-o9v: membership is the one place null behaves as a value rather than an absence - values_equal?(nil, nil) is true, so null in [null] is true even though null == null is :undefined (core/null-eq-null-propagates)
